question: Within the fully settled 283-archive state, did structural rejection remove the last observed usable checkpoint-derived support for any affected competition?

definitions.affected_competition: a distinct competition represented by at least one of the 14 structural-rejection events in the published census
definitions.retained_usable_support: the competition has accepted eligible runs in the prior anchor; archive-granularity retention supplies the exact support floor
definitions.invalid_only_trigger: the unique no-accepted-support competition is linked to the unique no-support rejection event, whose bound source archive has zero checkpoint runs and all discovered roots are live-only
definitions.observed_last_usable_support_elimination: a no-accepted-support affected competition whose linked rejected archive contains at least one checkpoint run

decision_rule.pass_if: all seven affected competitions are exhausted by retained_usable_support or invalid_only_trigger and observed_last_usable_support_elimination equals zero

claim_boundary.allowed: A within-state, identity-erased claim that the observed structural gate retained usable accepted support when it existed and otherwise rejected a uniquely linked archive with zero checkpoint runs.
forbidden: calling this new independent evidence or a fully blind confirmation
claiming future-corpus stationarity or a universal lossless validation theorem
claiming the malformed archive could not yield usable data after an untested repair
claiming predictor accuracy, scaling, search utility, causal method effect, or task whitelist/blacklist
